findings.about: Public comment from residents about tax bills and abatements
findings.official: several residents spoke stating their dissatisfaction, questions and concerns regarding tax bills and the abatement process.
findings.note: Our minutes cover discussion of abatements and resident questions in general terms, consistent with this summary; the official description is nonspecific.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted 3-0 to approve the Appellate Tax Board three-year average worksheet for abatements, the day before the filing deadline.
The principal assessor and a member said the board would make liberal use of its ability to extend the 90-day abatement deadlines.
Board members said they would accept added information on an abatement until it is decided, if the application is filed on time and notes more is coming.
The board declined to make an official statement of position on the waterfront assessments; a member gave a personal view that the system has flaws.
Motor vehicle excise abatements were signed; real estate exemptions are confidential and go to a future executive session.

why_it_matters: Owners who think a waterfront or lake assessment is too high can still file an abatement application by the deadline, and the board said it would accept supporting material afterward.
Residents asked for hearings, a position on the assessments and a look at the sales used in the valuation. The board made no commitment on any of these at this meeting.
watch_next: A future meeting where the board said it would take up formalizing the right to appear at abatement hearings.
A future executive session on real estate exemptions; the board meets monthly.
